content.jointProblem: Develop and test an unsupervised baseline-and-drift detector for Modbus/BACnet traffic that learns site-specific normal behaviour and raises explainable alerts; the first experiment will test whether SPC/change-point methods validated on sensor streams transfer to protocol-level traffic features without labelled attacks.

rationale.text: Ostojić has a directly relevant body of work on unsupervised and adaptive statistical monitoring for non-stationary industrial data.

sources.quote: Special attention is given to the interaction between control-chart theory and machine-learning approaches, including isolation forest, autoencoders, and one-class SVMs as anomaly scorers whose output feeds threshold-based alarms.

rationale.text: She has methods for online change-point detection in multivariate non-stationary streams, matching the need to learn a site-specific normal baseline that drifts.

sources.quote: This paper formulates a Bayesian online change-point detection model (BOCPD) extended to multivariate observations under a Normal-Inverse-Wishart conjugate prior.

rationale.text: Her work addresses calibration and threshold setting for one-class anomaly scores, which is central to controlling false alarms without labelled attacks.

sources.quote: Using a Platt-scaling calibration step and a bootstrap-based limit-setting procedure, the method achieves in-control ARLs within 5% of nominal across six simulated drift scenarios.

rationale.text: She has explicitly studied drift monitoring and recalibration of deployed anomaly detectors, which is needed for long-lived OT appliances.

sources.quote: proposes a two-level monitoring architecture in which a primary anomaly detector (isolation forest trained offline) is supervised by a secondary drift monitor based on the Page–Hinkley test

rationale.text: The group has taken drift-robust anomaly scoring into embedded deployment, relevant to ProtoSense on-device inference.

sources.quote: contributing drift-robust anomaly scoring modules certified to run on Cortex-M class microcontrollers.

rationale.text: She is open to joint projects and contract research with companies on anomaly detection and SPC system design.

sources.quote: joint research projects with companies operating sensor-instrumented production equipment
contract research on anomaly detection and SPC system design

rationale.text: Her published work links nonlinear anomaly detection to interpretable run-rule and average-run-length guarantees, which supports explaining alerts to a plant manager.

sources.quote: enabling the combination of nonlinear pattern recognition with the interpretability of run rules and average-run-length guarantees.

constraints.text: The detector must work without labelled malicious traffic and must not rely on supervised classifiers trained on public ICS datasets.

sources.quote: we have zero examples of malicious traffic and supervised classifiers are useless to us.
none of our clients has ever given us a packet capture that contains a confirmed attack.

constraints.text: The collaboration needs access to the client traffic archives and time-stamped operational data under NDA, because the researcher's group relies on real operational data.

sources.quote: access to our traffic archives, our hardware bench, and our existing firmware codebase under NDA
particularly interested in collaborators who can provide access to labelled or time-stamped operational data from real production systems

constraints.text: The method must cover Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic, not generic sensor streams.

sources.quote: passive protocol inspection module for Modbus TCP and BACnet/IP traffic

constraints.text: Alerts must be explainable to a plant manager in plain language and must avoid the false-alarm problem that caused clients to disable alerts.

sources.quote: We need a method that works with no attack examples and that we can explain to a plant manager in plain language.
flagged so many false positives in real deployments that clients started switching the alerts off.

constraints.text: Deployment must be lightweight on-device inference without affecting packet forwarding latency; the researcher can support only lightweight deployment of pre-trained models, not extensive embedded firmware development.

sources.quote: dedicated security processor to support on-device anomaly detection without affecting packet forwarding latency
She is not in a position to take on projects requiring extensive hardware integration or embedded firmware development beyond lightweight deployment of pre-trained models.

constraints.text: The company can dedicate only one to two engineers part-time, so the project plan must fit limited engineering capacity.

sources.quote: We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project

risks: . Transfer gap: Ostojić's empirical validations are on process/sensor time series, not Modbus/BACnet network traffic; the first experiment must test whether SPC/change-point features transfer to protocol traffic. Sources: SYN-PUB-08483.abstract quote "simulated batch reactor (50 process variables, 1 000 batches) as well as on data collected from a plastics-extrusion line"; SYN-PUB-08494.abstract quote "air-compressor units at a manufacturing plant".

No confirmed attacks means detection performance on real malicious Modbus/BACnet behaviour cannot be measured directly; evaluation will depend on synthetic, injected or maintenance-event proxies and may not generalise. Sources: C001-CH1.detail quotes "if they were compromised they would not know"; "but we have nothing labelled as malicious".

False-alarm tolerance is low because past supervised alerts were switched off; an unsupervised method may produce too many unexplained alerts in real sites. Source: C001-CH1.detail quote "clients started switching the alerts off".

Embedded integration risk: company firmware is C/Rust/Yocto and the researcher cannot take on extensive hardware/firmware work; a prototype may not reach ProtoSense without company engineering effort. Sources: C001.tech quotes "Embedded Linux (custom Yocto build)"; "C and Rust for firmware components"; R0773.notes quote about lightweight deployment only.

Researcher availability is unknown, and the company has only one engineer with six months of anomaly-detection reading and 1–2 part-time engineers, which may slow model development and evaluation. Sources: C001-CH1.detail quote "we have one engineer who has been reading about anomaly detection for six months"; C001.rd_capacity quote "We can dedicate one to two engineers part-time to a collaborative project".
questions: Can Prof. Ostojić confirm her availability and time commitment for a joint project, given that availability is currently unknown?
Would the company prefer a joint project or an industrial PhD track for one of its engineers, and is there a suitable candidate?
What NDA, client-consent and data-sharing terms apply to the traffic archives, and can the researcher access time-stamped captures from multiple sites?
Are there any maintenance logs, known incidents or operator annotations that can serve as retrospective validation events, even without confirmed attacks?
What are the deployment constraints on the planned fifth hardware variant: CPU/memory, allowed languages, inference latency budget and whether a Python/R prototype is acceptable before porting?
What false-alarm rate and alert-explainability format would plant managers and support staff accept?
Can the company provide hardware-in-the-loop PLC simulators and controlled Modbus/BACnet traffic for injecting synthetic anomalies?
Which Modbus/BACnet features or packet fields may be used, and are there privacy or regulatory limits on retaining or moving client traffic?
